lines.text: Paul and those with him put no obstacle in anyone's way, so that no one can discredit their ministry.
As servants of God, they commend themselves through endurance, shipwrecks, imprisonments, riots, sleepless nights, and hunger.
They serve in purity, knowledge, patience, and kindness, with the shield of faith in the right hand and the left.
They are viewed as imposters, yet genuine; sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; poor, yet making many rich.
Paul says their hearts are open wide, and as to his children he asks the Corinthians to open their hearts too.
